The presence of a well-defined mass in the diploic space of the left parietal bone, with sparse but preserved trabeculae and hyperintense foci on T1-weighted images presumed to represent bone marrow fat, is suggestive of a hemangioma. Although less likely, atypical fibroxanthoma is a consideration given the location of the mass in the parietal bone.
